title: Build the constant error carousel
brief: Implement an LSTM cell forward and backward and a GRU cell forward, then measure how far a pinned forget gate carries a gradient that a plain RNN would lose.
hints: Every gate is sigmoid(x @ W + h @ U + b) except the candidate, which uses tanh. Keep the same pre-activation pattern for all four LSTM gates and both GRU gates.
Store whatever lstm_cell_backward will need in the cache: x, h, c, the four gate arrays, c_new, and tanh(c_new). You will need every one of them.
The gradient reaching c_new from outside is dc_new plus the part that arrives through h_new: dc_total = dc_new + dh_new * o * (1 - tanh(c_new)**2).
Each gate's pre-activation gradient is its output gradient times its own local derivative: f * (1 - f) for the sigmoid gates, 1 - g**2 for the tanh candidate.

forget_gate_gradient_product is a cumulative product along the time axis: numpy.cumprod(forget_gates, axis=0) computes exactly the quantity the lesson derives for the cell-state Jacobian composed across steps.
